method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Post-exposure prophylaxis = thorough washing of wounds with soap plus the appropriate vaccine ± immunoglobulin regimen**, which prevents the virus entering the central nervous system.
claims.source_text: Post-exposure prophylaxis treatment with thorough washing of wounds with soap, as well as the appropriate vaccine ± immunoglobulin regimen, prevents virus entry into the central nervous system
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In Australia, exposure is from bats**, and in travellers returning from rabies-endemic areas.
claims.source_text: In Australia, exposure is from bats and travellers who have returned from rabies endemic areas
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Australian bat lyssavirus (ABLV) is closely related to rabies and is found in bats, including flying foxes and microbats. The disease caused by rabies and the other lyssaviruses is clinically indistinguishable.
claims.source_text: Australian Bat Lyssavirus (ABLV) is closely related to rabies and is found in bats (including flying foxes and microbats) … The clinical disease caused by rabies virus and the other lyssaviruses are indistinguishable and is termed “rabies”
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transmission is by bites, scratches, or direct viral contact with a mucosal surface**; human-to-human transmission is not proven. **Incubation ranges from 5 days to many years.**
claims.source_text: Transmission from animals to humans can occur as a result of bites or scratches from animals, or from direct viral contact with a mucosal surface. Transmission between humans has not been proven … Incubation period varies from 5 days to many years
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Advise families on prevention:** avoid contact with wildlife and vaccinate before travel to rabies-endemic areas.
claims.source_text: Advising families on prevention by avoiding contact with wildlife and undertaking vaccination prior to travelling to rabies endemic areas is extremely important
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History:** nature of exposure (bite, scratch, mucous membrane) · site (head and neck, highly innervated areas such as fingers) · animal source · country · first aid given · immunisation history (pre-exposure rabies prophylaxis, tetanus) · any rabies treatment given overseas — date, volume, type, route.
claims.source_text: Nature of exposure: bite, scratch, mucous membrane exposure Location of bite: head and neck, highly innervated areas eg fingers Animal source of exposure … Country of exposure First aid administered Immunisation history of the child (pre-exposure rabies prophylaxis, tetanus) Information on any rabies treatment given overseas; date, volume, type, route
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Within Australia, if a bat is the source and it can be done without putting others at risk, keep the bat for ABLV testing.**
claims.source_text: (note: within Australia if a bat is the source, and it is possible without placing others at risk, keep the bat to be sent for ABLV testing)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No investigations are needed for asymptomatic children.**
claims.source_text: No investigations are required for asymptomatic children
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **First aid: wash the wound with soap or detergent, flush it for 15 minutes, then apply an iodine-containing solution.** Appropriate first aid substantially reduces the infection risk.
claims.source_text: First aid: wash wound with soap or detergent then flush wound for 15 minutes. Apply an iodine-containing solution on top of the wound after flushing. Appropriate first aid substantially reduces the infection risk
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Open wound: clean ± debride — do not suture.**
claims.source_text: If the wound is open: clean ± debride, do not suture
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Category 2 bat exposures are managed differently from category 2 mammal exposures**, because superficial wounds from bats carry a higher infection risk.
claims.source_text: * Management of category 2 bat exposure is different to category 2 mammal exposure as superficial wounds from bats are a higher risk for infection
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If unsure whether treatment is needed, discuss with the local public health unit or health department, or the infectious diseases team.**
claims.source_text: If unsure whether treatment is required, discuss with local public health unit/health department or infectious diseases team
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give the first vaccine dose as soon as possible after exposure.** Check allergies: **Rabipur® contains egg protein.**
claims.source_text: The first dose of vaccine should be given as soon as possible after exposure … Check child’s allergies: the vaccine Rabipur® contains egg protein
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give the vaccine away from the HRIG site**, e.g. the contralateral deltoid or anterolateral thigh.
claims.source_text: Must be administered away from the site of HRIG eg contralateral deltoid or anterolateral thigh
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Rabies immunoglobulin (HRIG) 20 IU/kg.** Infiltrate as much of the dose as feasible in and around all wounds; **give the remainder IM in a different limb from the vaccine.**
claims.source_text: Rabies immunoglobulin (HRIG) dose 20 IU/kg … Infiltrate as much of the dose as possible in and around all wounds if feasible Give the remainder of the dose IM in a different limb from the rabies vaccine injection site
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **HRIG infiltration is painful — ensure adequate analgesia ± sedation.** Topical or local anaesthetic infiltration into the wound may dilute HRIG and lessen its effect; the evidence is uncertain.
claims.source_text: Infiltration of HRIG is painful, ensure adequate analgesia +/- sedation Topical and local anaesthetic (LA) infiltration into the wound may dilute HRIG and lessen its effectiveness; evidence for this is uncertain
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Immunocompromised children:** consult the Immunisation Handbook and the infectious diseases team for treatment and serological follow-up.
claims.source_text: Consult the immunisation handbook and infectious diseases team for treatment and serological follow-up of immunocompromised children
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PEP started overseas:** with clear documentation of an appropriate vaccine course, complete the standard regimen; if documentation is unclear, consult the Immunisation Handbook on whether to restart at Day 0.
claims.source_text: Post-exposure prophylaxis commenced overseas: If there is clear documentation of an appropriate vaccine course, complete treatment with the standard post-exposure prophylaxis regimen If there is unclear documentation or in other scenarios, consult the immunisation handbook as to whether the schedule should be restarted at Day 0
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Provision varies by state.** Victoria: give the family a patient-held record and order later doses through their nominated GP. NSW: Public Health Unit on 1300 066 055. QLD: contact the local Public Health Unit (case report form).
claims.source_text: Provision of treatment varies by state, check local information Victoria: provide the child/family with a patient held record and order subsequent vaccine doses to be given by their nominated GP NSW: contact local Public Health Unit on 1300 066 055 to arrange vaccine QLD: contact local Public Health Unit to arrange vaccine (Case report form)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Any confirmed case of rabies or ABLV requires urgent notification to the Department of Health.**
claims.source_text: Any confirmed cases of rabies or ABLV requires urgent notification to the Department of Health
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** a plan is in place to complete the vaccination schedule and review the wounds.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Plan is in place for completion of vaccination schedule and review of wounds
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Rabies and Australian bat lyssavirus post exposure prophylaxis' (Last updated December 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rabies_and_Australian_bat_lyssavirus_post_exposure_prophylaxis/, retrieved 2026-09-23
